name: Flexyne-GX
description: A transparent, ultra-thin graphene-polymer flexible electronics substrate developed by Tessera Materials for conformal circuit integration. Produced via roll-to-roll chemical vapor deposition onto a dissolvable polymer carrier, Flexyne-GX achieves sub-micron graphene layer uniformity across large sheet areas. Its near-perfect electron mobility and optical transparency make it the dominant substrate for wearable displays, skin-mounted biosensors, and flexible logic arrays.
story_hooks: A batch of Flexyne-GX biosensor patches sold through the Gray Zone-level black market vendors has been secretly modified to exfiltrate biometric data — whoever is behind it has access to Tessera's proprietary deposition process.
Flexyne-GX is being used as a substrate for illegal neural tap devices that bypass SNT interface protocols, creating an underground market for unregulated cognitive augmentation.
A Tier 2 street fabricator claims to have reverse-engineered a knockoff Flexyne-GX formula, threatening Tessera Materials' core revenue stream and drawing corporate enforcement down in the Gray Zone.
